FOREWORD This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards after the draft finalized by the Tobacco and Tobacco Products Sectional Committee had been approved by the Food and Agriculture Division Council. The leaves of Tendu tree ( Diospyrus melanoxylon Roxb. ) are used for wrapping bidis. They are obtained from mixed deciduous forests of the country and mainly found in Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Orissa, Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Gujarat, Kerala and Uttar Pradesh. This standard. would help the users in obtaining quality leaf, particularly as raw material for bidis. Tendu plants are pruned in the month of February and the mature leaves are collected after about 45 days. Leaves are bundled, each bundle containing 50 or 100 leaves called Pudas and then dried in sunlight for one week. The dried Pudas are sprinkled with water to soften them ( Bharti process ), then filled tightly in jute bags, exposed to direct sunlight for two days and stored till used. This standard been modified was first published in 1981. In this revision the packing to bring them in line with the current trade practices. and sampling requirements have

In the formulation of this standard, the committee has given due consideration to the prevailing trade practices in the country and the different grades prescribed under the Agricultural Produce ( Grading and Marking ) Act, 1937 and Rules framed thereunder. The provisions of packaging and marking are also subject to the requirements Standards of Weights and Measures ( Packaged Commodities ) Rules, 1977. stipulated under the

For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 `Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised )`. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

This standard prescribes the requirements different grades of Tendu leaves. 2 REFERENCE IS 4905 : 1968 `Methods for random sampling' is a necessary adjunct to this standard. 3 PHYSICAL 3.1 Description
Tendu leaves are large sized, usually 20 cm long and 10 cm wide, elliptical in shape, with narrow base and acute apex.

for

5.1 50 Tendu leaves are tied in bundles called Pudas for the drying process. Pudas are subjected to the Bharti process and then filled tightly in clean and sound jute bags. A bag containing 1 000 Pudas of 50 000 leaves is called as a Standard Bag. 5.2 The packages sealed properly. 6 MARKING Each bag shall be marked on each side with the following details: a) Description of contents, b) Name of the State/Forest of collection, c) Name of supplier, d) Grade designation, e) Net mass of contents, f)' Number of leaves per @da, and g) Date of packing. 7 STORAGE
Tendu leaves bags shall be stored in a clean and dry place away from moisture and heat.

A-1.3.2 The bundles from the gunny bags shall be selected at random. In order to ensure the randomness of selection, procedures given in IS 4905 : 1968 may be followed. A-2.1 From each of the bundles selected according to A-l.3 a Tendu leaf shall be picked up at random and examined for all the requirements of the specification. A Tendu leaf failing in one or more of the requirements shall be considered as defective. The lot shall be declared as conforming to the requirements of the specification if the number of defective Tendu leaves found in the sample is less than or equal to the corresponding acceptance number given in co1 3 of Table 2.

Standard Mark The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau 01 Indian Stan&r& Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The Standard Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well defined system of inspection, testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by BIS and operated by the producer. Standard marked products are also continuously checked by BIS for conformity to that standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the use of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufactures or producers may be obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards.
